title: Platform Oncall: Scenario Roulette & Failure Injection Catalog
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This document describes the 'Scenario Roulette' program: a curated, randomized failure-injection catalog and orchestration approach for platform oncall training, resilience verification, and continuous hardening of runtime operator playbooks. The goal is to simulate realistic multi-signal incidents against the LLM inference stack in a safe, observable, and replayable way.

Principles and scope

- Safety-first: every injection must have automated kill-switches, scoped impact windows, and pre-approved blast radius metadata.
- Repeatability: injections produce a deterministic run record (run_id) and artifact bundle for postmortem and metrics replay.
- Fidelity: scenarios mimic real failure signatures observed in production (latency spikes, KV cache corruption, model variant fallback misfires, token surges).
- Learning objective-driven: each roulette deck has explicit operator learning objectives and success criteria.
- Cost-aware: simulate economic effects (token burn, GPU preemption) in synthetic tenants where possible.

When to run

1. Quarterly operator training (mandatory for all platform oncall engineers).
2. Pre-major rollout rehearsal (canary or kernel changes).
3. Post-regression (after any cross-region incident >SLO-burn threshold).
4. Ad-hoc hardening experiments (by request from SRE/product).

Roles and ownership

- Program owner: Aisha Patel (Platform Resilience).
- Operator lead: oncall rotation engineer assigned to the gameday.
- Safety reviewer: SRE principal (approve blast radii and guardrails).
- Observability owner: dashboards team (ensure required panels are available).
- CI/CD owner: infra team (responsible for synthetic tenant seeding and cleanup).

Safety checklist (pre-run approvals)

1. Approval from Program owner + Safety reviewer (email + confluence approval macro).
2. Target environment verified: staging or isolated production slice.
3. Blast radius configured with safe tenants (list tenant IDs).
4. Automatic rollback and kill-switch endpoints validated.
5. Observability smoke tests green (dashboard query latencies < 10s).

Scenario deck structure

Each deck is a named collection of 3-7 injections with increasing complexity. A deck includes:
- deck_id (UUID)
- description and learning objectives
- expected duration (minutes)
- safe_tenants: list of tenant tags allowed for injection
- preconditions and synthetic workload profile
- runbook pointer and postmortem template

Example deck: "Model Swap Misfire Drill (deck_id: dcf3-4a21)"
- learning objectives: validate automatic fallback to quantized variant, assess downstream latency transparency, and practice customer notification.
- expected duration: 25 min
- safe_tenants: ["synthetic-e2e-1", "training-tenant-3"]

Failure injection catalog (representative entries)

1) Latency Warp: token-level tail latency injection
- id: LI-2026-01
- description: insert a synthetic latency distribution into the token generator path (90th/99th percentile inflation)
- impact: increased response time, partial SLO burn, potential operator paging
- parameters: duration_ms (2000), p95_multiplier (3), weight (0.4)
- guardrails: auto-disable after 10 minutes or when error rate > 2%
- observability signals: per-route latency, p99 token time, request tracing
- sample API payload:
  {
    \"injection_id\": \"LI-2026-01\",
    \"duration_s\": 600,
    \"targets\": [\"model-variant:rwkv-quant-8bit\"],
    \"profile\": {\"p95_mult\": 3, \"p99_mult\": 5}
  }

2) KV Prefix Corruption (non-destructive read-backoff)
- id: KV-2026-03
- description: simulate partial corruption of a single KV prefix shard with bounded TTL inconsistencies
- impact: higher model cold starts, cache miss ratio spike
- parameters: shard_id, corruption_window_s (300)
- guardrails: only affects synthetic shard IDs, automatic prefix-redirect to fallback store after 30s
- observability signals: kv-hitratio, warmstart-count, cold-start-duration

3) Model Variant Swap Failure (atomic mis-swap)
- id: MS-2026-07
- description: emulate canary rollout misconfiguration that swaps a model variant without proper config; results in model mismatch errors for a subset of routes
- impact: request errors (400/5xx), degraded quality, potential customer-facing incidents
- parameters: affected_routes (list), error_type (mismatch|timeout), throttle_percent (10)
- guardrails: immediate rollback trigger when error-rate > threshold or on manual abort

4) Token Surge Flood (synthetic tenant)
- id: TS-2026-09
- description: inject a sustained token generation surge from a synthetic tenant to test autoscaler fairness and billing pipelines
- impact: burst scaling, cost signals, throttling behavior validation
- parameters: qps, sustained_duration_s, tenant_tag
- guardrails: quota enforcement and token burn cap (configurable per run)

Execution workflow (operator-facing)

1. Preflight (10–20 min)
  a. Confirm run_id and deck selection
  b. Validate all safety checks (see Safety checklist)
  c. Seed synthetic tenants and baseline traces
  d. Notify stakeholders via incident channel with plan and abort code
2. Inject (0–5 min per injection)
  a. Trigger injection using CLI or Injection Service API (example below)
  b. Watch key dashboards and traces for immediate anomalies
  c. If abnormal failure beyond blast radius: hit kill-switch and document time
3. Observe & Triage (during and 20 min after)
  a. Follow runbook steps for detected alerts: escalate to ownership teams as listed in runbook
  b. Practice operator actions (rollback, model-swap, cache-warmup)
4. Clean up and artifact collection (5–15 min)
  a. Stop scenario and verify return-to-normal metrics
  b. Archive run bundle (run_id, traces, logs, dashboards snapshots)
  c. Fill out postmortem template

Injection Service CLI examples

- Trigger an injection (curl)
curl -X POST https://injection-service.internal/api/v1/inject \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROULETTE_TOKEN' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{ "injection_id": "LI-2026-01", "targets": ["model-variant:rwkv-quant-8bit"], "duration_s": 300, "run_id": "roulette-20260214-08" }'

- Kill switch (safe abort)
curl -X POST https://injection-service.internal/api/v1/abort \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROULETTE_TOKEN' \\n  -d '{"run_id": "roulette-20260214-08"}'

Dashboard & alert requirements

Minimum dashboard panels for any deck run:
- Run overview (run_id, deck_id, start_time, operator, status)
- Token-level latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) by route and model variant
- KV hit ratio and warmstart counts by prefix shard
- Error-rate by route, with attack injection tag filtering
- Autoscaler actions and GPU utilization
- Token burn by tenant and cumulative cost estimate

Suggested alerting adjustments during runs (temporary mute/route-specific):
- Suppress customer-facing pager noise by routing alerts to the gameday channel and annotate with run_id
- Keep SLO burn monitors active but mark as 'training' to avoid infra escalations unless thresholds exceed emergency level

Sample dashboard JSON snippet (Grafana panel minimal example)
{\n  \"panel\": {\n    \"title\": \"KV Hit Ratio (run_id: {run_id})\",\n    \"targets\": [{ \"expr\": \"sum(rate(kv_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_requests[5m]))\" }],\n    \"span\": 6\n  }\n}

Postmortem & retro format

- Objective: capture what we learned and update operator runbooks and automation.
- Template fields (populate in Confluence):
  1. run_id, deck_id, operator(s), date/time
  2. scenario sequence and parameter values
  3. timeline of notable events (with UTC times)
  4. observations: metrics that crossed thresholds, signal-to-action latency
  5. What went well / What surprised us
  6. Action items (ownership and due dates)
  7. Runbook updates required
  8. Regression test plan to ensure changes are covered by CI-simulations

Example retrospective prompts

- Did any dashboard panels fail to surface the needed signal? Which queries were slow or missing?
- How long between alert and effective mitigation? Were operator steps clearly visible in the runbook?
- Any automation misfires (e.g., mutated rollout policies)?
- What low-hanging improvements to observability or automation would prevent manual steps?

Failure classification matrix (quick lookup)

| Failure class | Primary signal | Immediate operator action | Escalation|
|---|---:|---|---|
| Latency Warp | p99 latency up 3x | Validate injection, check autoscaler, consider throttle | Platform SRE
| KV Corruption | kv-hitratio drop 40% | Trigger fallback, rebuild prefix, monitor warmstarts | Storage / Runtime
| Model Mis-swap | route error-rate > 1% | Rollback variant; tag affected routes; invalidate caches | Model Onboarding Team
| Token Surge | sustained qps spike | Engage quota throttle; reassign burst credits | Capacity Planning

Operational automation priorities (next 12 months)

- Implement pre-run automatic tenant isolation (reduce manual seeding).
- Add per-injection cost estimate to run preview to allow budget-aware decisions.
- Expand injection library with network partition simulation and kernel-level scheduler perturbation.
- Integrate injection run metadata into incident review pipeline for cross-run analytics.

Appendix A — Deck examples (short)

- "Warmset Evacuation" (tests graceful eviction and rebalance)
- "Canary Roll Swap" (model variant atomicity failures)
- "Billing Spike" (token surge and cost telemetry pipeline validation)

Appendix B — Run tagging conventions

- run_id format: roulette-YYYYMMDD-XX (e.g., roulette-20260214-08)
- deck tags: deck:<deck_id>, objective:<short-tag>
- artifact bundle: run_id-artifacts.tar.gz stored in s3://platform-roulette/archives/
